page: Microsoft Azure E48s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, the instance delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory footprint totals 384.0 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Local ephemeral disk storage is not bundled, requiring reliance on network-attached storage architectures compatible with Premium Storage. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs or hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate upper-quartile performance for memory and encryption tasks. The instance placed in the top 25 percent for PassMark memory score (2870.18), PassMark database operations (21815.19), and PassMark CPU encryption (42905.02), supported by hardware-level AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. Compute benchmarks, including multi-core stress-ng (46608.74) and Geekbench multi-core (15644.0), align within the average 50 percent band. Without discrete accelerators, large-model machine learning generation is constrained, scoring in the lowest 10 percent on large language model 70B text generation.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides resource efficiency for configurations constrained by memory limits rather than raw compute cycles. With verified performance in transactional database metrics, the server fits large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-capacity ETL pipelines, and memory-bound enterprise applications backed by remote storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E48s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine providing 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system features an 8.0 GB per-vCPU allocation, catering to workloads with substantial memory demands. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached Premium Storage for persistent data, and the instance includes no GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles reveal upper-quartile results in memory bandwidth, database operations, and cryptographic workloads, while general compute metrics perform within the middle tier. In-flight instruction extensions include AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI. Given its memory capacity and absence of internal disks, the E48s_v5 is best configured for distributed in-memory caching, large enterprise relational databases, and memory-intensive batch processing pipelines.
